project_tracker_diagnostic: Annual; finely divided lower leaves and narrower upper leaves; yellow rays often with dark maroon basal blotches; pappus reduced to short scales/awns.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common and useful Central Texas field-learning taxon.

morphology_keys.leaves: Lower leaves deeply divided into narrow segments; upper leaves opposite to alternate and less dissected.
morphology_keys.heads: Rays yellow, commonly with dark reddish-brown blotches near the base; disks dark yellow to brownish.
morphology_keys.phyllaries: Outer involucre of narrow bracts beneath broader inner phyllaries.
morphology_keys.fruit: Cypselae flattened, typically with 2 short awns and small marginal teeth/scales.
best_field_traits: Longer outer calyculus bractlets beneath a mature head (usually 6–9 mm in FNA; photograph side/underside with scale).
Longer inner phyllaries (usually 7–9+ mm) and relatively long head stalks (6–15+ cm).
Basal/cauline leaves simple or 1–2-pinnately lobed with relatively broad terminal lobes; assess several leaves, not a single unusual one.
Yellow rays often with a reddish-brown basal spot or band, supportive only and shared with C. tinctoria.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against Coreopsis tinctoria: compare OUTER head bractlets first (C. basalis usually 6–9 mm; C. tinctoria 1–3+ mm), inner phyllaries (7–9+ versus 4–7[–9] mm), and head stalks (6–15+ versus usually 1–5 cm). C. tinctoria usually has more finely divided stem leaves with narrow threadlike lobes. Flower color alone overlaps. Central Texas narrow-leaved C. basalis can resemble historical C. wrightii concepts; do not force a separate name without taxonomy review.

look_here_first: Start below a mature flower head: measure the long, narrow OUTER involucral bracts (calyculus; usually 6–9 mm), then the inner phyllaries (about 7–9+ mm). Check the mostly simple or few-lobed lower leaves and long bare head stalk (peduncle; often 6–15+ cm). Dark red at the ray bases is NOT enough: plains coreopsis (C. tinctoria) can share that color.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against Coreopsis tinctoria: compare OUTER head bractlets first (C. basalis usually 6–9 mm; C. tinctoria 1–3+ mm), inner phyllaries (7–9+ versus 4–7[–9] mm), and head stalks (6–15+ versus usually 1–5 cm). C. tinctoria usually has more finely divided stem leaves with narrow threadlike lobes. Flower color alone overlaps. Central Texas narrow-leaved C. basalis can resemble historical C. wrightii concepts; do not force a separate name without taxonomy review.

look_alikes.separate_by: Measure outer calyculus bractlets and inspect several cauline leaves; small bractlets and threadlike segments favor C. tinctoria.
look_alikes.caution: Both can have yellow rays with red-brown basal markings; never identify from flower color alone.

look_alikes.separate_by: Some narrow-leaved western C. basalis have been treated under this name; refer naming decisions to taxonomy lane.
look_alikes.caution: Taxon-concept comparison, not proof of a distinct local species.
